capstone-fde/module-1-fullstack-commerce.summary: Build and verify the commerce backbone—React storefront, FastAPI services, and PostgreSQL—before any AI layers.

sections.heading: What we will do
sections.body:
- Stand up one e-commerce application skeleton: product catalog, product detail, cart, checkout, and order history.
- Connect FastAPI routes to PostgreSQL so lists, carts, and orders reflect real persisted data.
- Wire the React client to those APIs with loading, empty, and error states.
- Prove the customer shopping journey works end-to-end while the assistant features are still off.
- Record what is verified vs. still rough so later modules add AI without masking broken commerce.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body:
- How FDEs **stabilize core product flows** before adding LLM complexity.
- FastAPI resource design for catalog, cart, and orders with validation.
- React patterns for API-backed UI states.
- PostgreSQL as the source of truth for storefront data.
- Trade-offs when introducing AI on top of an untested vs. tested commerce stack.

objectives: Explain the end-to-end shopper flow in one diagram or short narrative
Name the FastAPI routes and tables that back catalog, cart, and orders
Describe how UI states map to API success, empty, and failure
State why commerce must work before agents or RAG are added

capstone-fde/module-2-multi-agent-store-.summary: Layer a LangGraph multi-agent assistant on the same storefront—store actions with clear permissions, not open-ended chat.

sections.heading: What we will do
sections.body:
- Define shopper questions the assistant should handle: product search, cart status, order lookup.
- Start from a single-agent baseline on existing store tools, then split responsibilities into specialists.
- Design an orchestrator that routes to Product Search, Cart, and Order agents with **scoped** database permissions.
- Implement a LangGraph flow with conditional routing and minimal context between nodes.
- Test invalid questions, unauthorized actions, and failures against normal app behavior.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body:
- When a **single agent** is enough vs. when **multi-agent** routing improves control.
- LangGraph orchestration and specialist boundaries in a production-shaped app.
- Tool design that reuses FastAPI and database access—no duplicate business logic.
- Permission models for agents that can read or mutate store data.
- Failure behavior: refuse, escalate, or hand off without corrupting cart or orders.

objectives: Map example shopper questions to the correct specialist agent
Explain what each agent may read or change in the database
Contrast single-agent limits with multi-agent routing benefits
List failure cases where the assistant must not guess or over-act

capstone-fde/module-3-agentic-rag-produc.summary: Add agentic RAG over approved product manuals—cited answers about products without letting retrieval mutate the cart.

sections.heading: What we will do
sections.body:
- Curate approved product documentation (manuals, specs, warranty notes) with clear ownership.
- Chunk, embed, and index content in **ChromaDB** with metadata tied to products.
- Build an agentic retrieval loop: query preparation, sufficiency checks, grounded answers with **quotes**, and explicit refusal when evidence is weak.
- Expose a manual-assistance mode in the UI separate from store-action chat.
- Evaluate ambiguous questions and attacks where retrieval must not invent specs or change orders.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body:
- **Agentic RAG** vs. one-shot retrieval for product Q&A.
- ChromaDB collections, metadata, and citation discipline in customer-facing apps.
- Separating **store mutations** (agents) from **read-only knowledge** (RAG).
- Refusal and low-confidence behavior as product requirements.
- Connecting observability from Section 2 to capstone retrieval quality.

objectives: Describe the document sources and how chunks map to products
Explain citation and refusal rules in plain language
State why RAG endpoints must not perform cart or checkout actions
Name metrics or traces that show retrieval quality

capstone-fde/module-4-deployment-and-dem.summary: Ship a pilot-ready demo: repeatable runs, a cloud URL, smoke tests, and a concise handover story.

sections.heading: What we will do
sections.body:
- Package the unified app for repeatable local and container runs.
- Promote a POC build to a hosted URL with secrets outside source control.
- Run smoke tests on commerce, agent store actions, and manual RAG modes.
- Prepare a short demo narrative: what works, known gaps, and operational limits.
- Align handover artifacts with deployment and observability practices from earlier stages.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body:
- FDE deployment habits: env config, health checks, rollback thinking.
- How to demo **three modes** in one app without confusing stakeholders.
- Smoke-test design for full-stack plus AI surfaces.
- Honest gap lists vs. overselling pilot features.
- Sponsor-ready storytelling for integrated commerce, agents, and RAG.

objectives: List environments from local dev through POC URL
Name smoke tests that prove commerce and both assistant modes
Summarize risks and known gaps for a five-minute readout
Connect capstone demo to production-hardening themes from Section 2
